questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: History of the city and there academic reputation for future applications in academia

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a great exchange. Met a lot of wonderful people, but it is difficult to make local friends as they are younger and don't really want to make friends with many exchange students as we are leaving 4 months later.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The city is self is a climb with three bags though, so be ready!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: there is almost always someone to ask about direction and location. The geoscience exchange coordinator in Edinburgh were really nice and the check up was easy. She also responded really fast via. email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: you can apply through the university but you have to do it as quickly as you can. It is not guarantied to 1 semester students, so not a lot is available, but I lived on Nicolson St and it was nice and right in the center of the city. The whole city is the campus. Getting accommodation elsewhere is difficult, but doable.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: My place had a kitchen which I shared with 3 roommates. if you stay at Pollock then it is catered.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They don't like that you put stuff on the walls. It was good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was lucky to get something, but it has been difficult to find living places for my friends that didn't get anything from the University.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything was sent in emails, so it was pretty easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Lots of steps to fill out, but not very difficult. It's pretty standard I think, but I did it last year, so I don't remember.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Funny enough it was easier and faster to get a respond from the exchange people in Edinburgh then getting ahold of someone at KU.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. Got everything I wanted and was lucky enough that nothing clashed with each other, but heard from friends that changing courses in the first 2 weeks is easy enough. Just find the email to your tutor (didn't have one) or send an email to the institution you are under.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it in good time and don't be afraid to send them as many emails as you need, cause they most likely have the answer you are looking for. For housing through the university do it as quickly as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of self study going on and the lectures in one of my courses was online because the prof didn't like the classroom we were assigned and he couldn't get another. But the level was good. Learned a lot!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Glacial proccesses and geomorphology. 3rd year course (I think)
Global environmental change - Foundations (3 year course) but the prof kept referring to an oceanology course they had the year before, but wasn't a requirement, so that was annoying as it wasn't disclosed in the course introduction online. 
Natural Hazards (2 year), but a lot of first year take is as well. I have mixed feelings about this course as the practicals were easy, but the exam was a mystery that I didn't feel properly prepared for.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: teaching style is pretty similar, but the practicals were more hand in based. The exam was way different. Had one 24-hour exams and two written-exams (2-hours), but they do it on paper. Wasn't ready for that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Glacial proccesses and geomorphology
Global environmental change - Foundations
Natural Hazards

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Glacial processes was really good as we don't have anything like it at home.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: the rent wasn't stretched out over 4 months but 3, so it was more per month than expected. The transport via busses is cheap and easy as you can pay with Apple Pay fx.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
housing because of the way they did it. 
Ended up using 10.000 kr from my savings, but I think its ok.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were loads but didn't sign up for anything.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Soooo many. In the first week there is a event where all the societies have a booth, so you can see what is available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did the scandinavian society, which was fun! loads of events, but the university also hold events that you can join. There is typically a little fee, but hasn't been over 20 pounds I think! Go to a Ceilidh! its a traditional scottish event and its so fun!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: see the highlands or maybe just the Pentland Hills! its closer and soooo beautiful. Climb Arhtur's seat at least once and just explore Edinburgh! its a beautiful city!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. Its just the UK, so the difference isn't that big. But the food... I was craving rugbrød sooo badly in the end.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: its difficult, but should be doable. My friends were primarily other exchange students, but join societies is an easy way in!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I just love the UK, so I thought it was all great to some extend, but again the food. If you don't want to eat out then get creative. But again I'm a lousy cook.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for student accommodation quickly 
Remember to make time for exploring outside the city! Join the Erasmus trips! didn't manage to get tickets. 
Go to the law library when they open during the exam season! Get there 15 min before, so you can get a seat! its the prettiest library and makes you feel important and capable of crushing your exams.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just take time to enjoy yourself! go to different cities! Go to Durham, it is soooo beautiful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friendships and academic experience from a top UK university!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam season is the longest 3 weeks of your life! remember to enjoy the small moments during that time!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
